Expecting 9-12 months, with the opportunity to move to full-time. Hours: 8 hours a day, but can flex.
Hourly rate: $26-48 hourly About Engram Biosciences (https://www.engram.co/)

Engram Biosciences is building an autonomous brain organoid platform to improve how neurological diseases are studied and how potential therapies are discovered. Our long-term vision is to dramatically increase success in neurology by generating more informative, reproducible data from human biology.
We combine human iPSC-derived brain models with automation, high-content imaging, electrophysiology, and single-cell and spatial measurements. Consistent, well-characterized brain organoids are central to that work.

About the contract role

We are seeking a hands-on Research Associate for an on-site contract position focused primarily on producing and characterizing 3D human brain organoids, including forebrain and other region-specific models. You will maintain the stem cell cultures that support organoid production, monitor organoids through development, and help improve consistency between batches.
You will also support related neural cell models and assays, working closely with colleagues in biology, imaging, and automation. This is a bench-focused Research Associate role suited to someone with a bachelor’s degree and strong practical experience; a master’s degree is welcome but not required.

What you’ll do

Maintain human iPSCs and neural stem or progenitor cells, including passaging, banking, cryopreservation, and routine quality checks.
Generate and maintain forebrain and other region-specific brain organoids using established differentiation protocols.
Monitor organoid morphology, health, maturation, and variation within and between batches.
Induce and work with glial lineages, such as astrocytes, microglia, or oligodendrocytes, to support neural model development and characterization.
Prepare cultures and organoids for staining, imaging, and other downstream assays.
Document cell lines, organoid batches, culture conditions, deviations, and results clearly; help troubleshoot and refine protocols.
Support 2D neuronal cultures where they contribute to development or evaluation of the 3D models.

What you bring

A bachelor’s degree in neuroscience, stem cell biology, cell biology, bioengineering, or a related field. A master’s degree is also acceptable.
Hands-on experience with human iPSC culture and 3D brain organoid differentiation or maintenance, ideally including forebrain or other region-specific models.
Must have hands-on iPSC cell culture experience; brain organoid experience is ideal.
Experience maintaining neural stem or progenitor cells and strong aseptic technique.
Hands-on glial lineage induction experience with at least one of astrocytes, microglia, or oligodendrocytes.
Careful experimental execution, clear documentation, and the ability to recognize and troubleshoot culture variability.

Additional experience we value

Inhibitory neuron induction; single-cell library preparation using 10x Genomics, Parse Biosciences, or Fluent BioSciences workflows; experience with using high-content imagers like Molcular Device’s ImageXpress; and exposure to laboratory automation.

On-site amenities and contract terms

On-site amenities include delivered lunch, snacks, and complimentary access to a state-of-the-art gym. The contract duration, pay rate, and eligibility for insurance or retirement benefits should be stated once the engagement terms are set.

Job Description

Idaho National Laboratory is hiring a well-qualified Postdoctoral Research Associate in Computational Geoscience for the Department of Critical Minerals & Geothermal Energy in the Energy and Environment Science and Technology (EES&T) directorate. This postdoctoral researcher will advance reactive transport and coupled thermal–hydraulic–mechanical–chemical (THMC) simulations emphasizing interactions among fluid flow, heat transfer, geochemical reactions, geomechanics, and evolving rock properties. Simulations will be developed using FALCON (Fracturing And Liquid CONvection) and MOOSE (Multiphysics Object-Oriented Simulation Environment), or similar tools. Research will address geological hydrogen (geohydrogen) production, electrofracturing stimulation for critical mineral recovery, enhanced geothermal systems (EGS), and carbon mineralization. Our team works a 9x80 schedule with every other Friday off.

Key Responsibilities

Develop reactive transport models using FALCON/MOOSE or similar tools, coupling advection, diffusion, dispersion, aqueous speciation, and mineral dissolution and precipitation with thermal, hydraulic, and mechanical processes.
Implement reaction kinetics and reactive surface area, porosity, permeability, and fracture–matrix exchange conditions; quantify species transport and elemental mass balances. Evaluate transport-limited versus reaction-limited behavior and represent mineralogical heterogeneity and evolving fluid chemistry across laboratory and reservoir scales.
Model hydrogen generation through water–rock reactions, critical mineral mobilization and recovery, and carbon mineralization; evaluate how fluid chemistry and operating conditions influence reaction progress and recovery.
Couple electrofracturing and electrohydraulic stimulation with reactive transport to assess fracture connectivity, fluid access, and mineral accessibility; simulate circulation and heat extraction in EGS.
Verify numerical implementations, calibrate and validate models against laboratory or field observations, and assess convergence, parameter sensitivity, and uncertainty.
Automate computational workflows, improve parallel performance, collaborate with experimental teams, publish findings, and contribute to research proposals.

The candidate is expected to be a strong asset to our interdisciplinary R&D team and work effectively both alone and as a team member. The candidate must be self-motivated but also take direction from other team members and peers.

The position entails writing scientific manuscripts for journal publication, and presentation of research results at national and international conferences and meetings.

Required

PhD in Geoscience, Geochemistry, Engineering, Materials Science, Computational Science, or a related discipline.
PhD requirements must be completed by commencement of appointment and within the previous 5 years.
Hands-on multiphysics modeling experience using FALCON/MOOSE or similar tools, with understanding of porous-media flow and coupled THMC processes. Demonstrated ability to couple multiple physical processes and interpret chemical and hydrological feedback is essential.
Foundation in finite-element methods and nonlinear numerical solution techniques, with experience in model verification or validation.
Scientific programming in C++, Fortran, Python, or MATLAB, with ability to develop, adapt, and maintain numerical modeling components and automated simulation workflows.
A developing peer-reviewed publication record, effective communication, and ability to conduct independent research within interdisciplinary teams.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

Experience with FALCON and MOOSE Porous Flow, Geochemistry, Solid Mechanics, or Phase Field capabilities, including coupling THMC processes.
Experience with phase-field fracture, damage mechanics, constitutive model development, or fracture-dependent permeability, particularly for brittle geomaterials and hydraulic or electrically driven stimulation.
Experience simulating reactive transport models, familiarity with thermodynamic databases, kinetic rate laws, and the influence of temperature and fluid composition on mineral reactivity is desirable.
Experience with nonlinear solvers, Newton’s or quasi-Newton’s methods, sparse linear algebra, preconditioning, and parallel programming using the Message Passing Interface (MPI). Proficiency with Python scientific libraries; familiarity with COMSOL Multiphysics for complementary simulations and benchmarking.

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this classification, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, stoop, kneel, bend. The job requires hand/finger dexterity to keyboard or type, handle materials, manipulate tools, and reach with hands and arms. The job requires operation of job-related equipment. jobs.description:
Themis Bios is building the measurement layer for modern biology. Our single-cell RNA-seq technology is designed to make transcriptomic readouts routine, quantitative, and scalable — so scientists can ask harder questions and trust the answers.

We are looking for a Research Associate or Senior Research Associate to join Applications Development and own the cell biology at the front of our workflows. This is a hands-on, bench-first role: you will grow the cells, build the models, and turn living systems into single-cell samples that read cleanly on our platform. Your first focus is the Evidence Base: running the drug-perturbation experiments behind a growing atlas of how human primary cells and organoids respond to compounds. You will work alongside our Product Development team, and your culture work and sample prep will be the foundation the rest of the applications work is built on.

It is a good fit for someone who takes real pride in cell culture and technique, wants their bench work to feed a product, and brings hands-on drug screening experience they want to build on with single-cell readouts.

What you'll do
Cell culture.
Culture primary human PBMCs (thaw, rest and T-cell activation, e.g. anti-CD3/CD28) and gut organoids, with iPSC-derived models as needed — covering media preparation, plating, passaging, expansion, and cryopreservation, all under strict sterile technique.
Model quality.
Monitor culture health, morphology, and consistency; run routine checks and keep cultures to documented, reproducible standards so downstream results are trustworthy.
Sample preparation.
Prepare single-cell and single-nucleus samples from cells, organoids, and tissue — dissociation, viability and debris management, counting, and input QC — tuned for compatibility with the Themis scRNA-seq technology.
Experiment execution.
Execute cell-culture and sample-prep experiments, and run drug-perturbation studies (drug and molecule treatments across dose and time), under the direction of senior team members.
Drug plate preparation.
Prepare compound stocks in DMSO, serial dilutions, dose–response and combination layouts, and randomized plate maps with vehicle and control wells; keep compound inventory, storage and lot records current.

Program and run liquid handlers (e.g. Agilent Bravo) for plate stamping, dilution and sample handling, and keep run logs.
Screening cadence.
Deliver about two drug plates a week on schedule, from cells to single-cell libraries, with QC at each step.
Data and records.
Generate high-quality, reproducible data and keep detailed, well-organized experimental records.
Protocols and QC.
Help turn working procedures into clear protocols and SOPs, and contribute to input-QC and sample-acceptance methods as workflows mature.
Lab operations.
Keep the lab running — inventory, reagent and consumable stocks, equipment upkeep and calibration — so experiments start on time and run clean.

What you'll bring
Bachelor's or Master's degree in cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, or a related field.
2–5 years of relevant industry or advanced academic laboratory experience (toward the upper end for the SRA level).
Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture skills and disciplined sterile technique — together with drug screening, this is the core of the role.
Hands-on drug or compound screening in mammalian cells — dose–response or plate-based assays, including preparing drug plates from stocks.
Experience with primary immune cells (PBMCs preferred) and one or more of: 3D / organoid culture, or iPSC culture and differentiation.
Sample-prep experience — dissociating cells, organoids, or tissue into high-quality single-cell suspensions, or a clear aptitude to learn it quickly.
Careful technique with complex biological workflows, and a track record of generating reproducible data and troubleshooting experiments.
Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and clear documentation habits.
Comfortable in a dynamic startup environment with evolving priorities.

Strongly preferred
Experience with single-cell genomics workflows (e.g. scRNA-seq, droplet or bead-based systems, barcoding / cell-hashing methods).
Experience writing or adapting liquid-handler methods (e.g. Agilent Bravo, Hamilton, Echo) or other high-throughput sample handling.

Nice to have
Experience with NGS library prep and QC methods (Bioanalyzer, TapeStation, Qubit, fragment analysis).
Basic data-analysis skills (e.g. Python, R, or standard analysis tools) for exploring experimental results.
Prior work in an assay-development, applications, or product-development lab.

What success looks like
Cultures and models are healthy, consistent, and ready when the team needs them.
Single-cell samples go into the workflow at high quality, with QC that holds up run to run.
Data is reproducible and records are clear enough that others can build on the work.

Research Associate / Associate Scientist, Data Generation

Divergence Labs is hiring a full-time Research Associate / Associate Scientist to run the laboratory data generation work that feeds our machine learning models for antibody and biologics design. We are seeking a capable candidate with a track record of scientific and professional achievement, including but not limited to 1 – 3 years of academic or industry experience in a molecular biology or protein science laboratory. The role is based on-site in San Francisco, CA, and works directly with our Machine Learning and Engineering team.

Divergence Labs is a biotechnology company on a mission to reshape standard of care across all disease areas. Founded in 2025 by an interdisciplinary team of biotechnology investors, drug hunters, hardware engineers, and machine learning scientists, we have assembled a high-performance team that unites investment acumen, world-class protein engineering, advanced computational research, and translational medicine to build repeatable methods for discovering new medicines which transform patient care. Divergence has presence across San Francisco, CA, Minneapolis, MN, New York, NY, and Cambridge, UK. Although we have not publicly disclosed our financing details, Divergence is well capitalized and backed by world-leading investors, each of whom are among the earliest investors in companies such as Isomorphic Labs, Xaira Therapeutics, Coefficient Bio/Anthropic, and Chai Discovery, among others. We are among a select set of biotechnology companies with a strategic relationship with Anthropic.

We are committed to identifying, developing, and rewarding world-class talent, and, as such, all positions at Divergence Labs come with market-leading compensation.

The Role

We are hiring a hands-on Research Associate / Associate Scientist to be the experimental half of our design loop in San Francisco. Our machine learning team designs antibodies computationally; this role turns those designs into physical molecules and measured data, and returns that data to the models that learn from it. The San Francisco group is small and tightly coupled: machine learning scientists, software engineers and hardware engineers working alongside the bench scientists who generate the experimental readouts their models depend on.

You will work day to day at the bench running our data generation pipeline: building designed sequences from synthetic DNA, expressing the encoded proteins, and measuring binding. The quality, consistency and turnaround of what you produce sets the pace for model development and pipeline execution, and the people who use your data one desk away.

This is also a role with room to grow. You will be trained on our core methods, work closely with engineers who are automating them, and have the opportunity to take on greater ownership of assay development, automation and data analysis as the pipeline scales.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are looking for a capable, motivated bench scientist who wants to learn fast in a small, integrated team and contribute from day one. Your background should include:

Solid hands-on molecular biology and protein experience
: Confident and independent at the bench with routine molecular biology, protein expression and plate-based assays, executed consistently and on schedule.
A data-minded, reliable working style
: You treat every plate as a dataset someone else will train on: consistent execution, careful controls and records, and problems flagged and troubleshooted.
Curiosity about machine learning and automation
: Keen to work at the interface of the bench and the model, and to grow into greater ownership as the pipeline scales.

Key Responsibilities

Run the data generation pipeline
: Execute our build-and-test workflow end to end, from synthetic DNA through expressed protein to binding measurements, on a regular weekly cadence.
Build designed sequences
: Carry out the molecular biology that turns computational designs into testable constructs: PCR, assembly, pooled and arrayed library handling, and sequence verification.
Express and quantify proteins
: Produce antibody fragments and target antigens in small-scale, plate-based formats, and confirm expression and quality before measurement.
Measure binding at scale
: Run high-throughput binding and kinetics assays (e.g., biolayer interferometry), including instrument setup, controls, and first-pass data review.
Deliver clean, structured data
: Record sample tracking, metadata and results in the formats our machine learning team consumes, and flag failed or ambiguous runs before they reach a model.
Operate and help improve automation
: Run liquid handlers and plate-based instruments, and work with our engineers to raise throughput, reduce cost per datapoint and shorten turnaround.
Troubleshoot and iterate
: Identify the source of failed runs, test fixes, and help refine protocols and SOPs as methods mature.
Keep the lab running
: Prepare reagents, manage consumables and ordering, maintain shared equipment, and coordinate with external vendors where needed.
Embody good lab citizenship
: Maintain lab cleanliness and organization and comply with local SOPs and health-and-safety requirements.

Required Experience

Successful candidates will have a BSc or MSc in molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering or a related discipline, plus 1 – 3 years of hands-on laboratory experience in an industry or academic research setting.

The candidate must have:
Practical molecular biology experience: PCR, cloning or DNA assembly, gel electrophoresis, plasmid preparation and sequence verification.
Working experience with protein expression and with plate-based assays in 96- or 384-well format.
Careful, organized documentation habits: accurate record-keeping, sample tracking and comfort working to established SOPs.
Comfort with data: able to organize results in spreadsheets, review them for quality and spot when something looks wrong.
A genuine desire to be in the lab: hands-on, rigorous, and happy for the majority of your time to be at the bench.
Good interpersonal and communication skills, appropriate for a small, integrated team where cross-domain conversation happens daily, and the confidence to ask questions and raise issues early.
Motivation to excel in a fast-moving environment: comfortable with shifting priorities and a weekly experimental cadence.

Additional Experience Welcomed

Not required, but candidates with one or more of the following will be at an advantage:

Experience with binding/kinetics measurement: biolayer interferometry (Octet/Gator), SPR, or similar.
Experience with liquid handlers and laboratory automation (e.g., Opentrons, Hamilton).
Experience with oligo pools, pooled libraries, or cell-free protein expression.
Experience with antibodies, VHHs or other biologics, including small-scale purification and QC.
Familiarity with next-generation sequencing sample preparation.
Basic scripting in Python or R for data handling, or a strong interest in learning.
Experience with electronic lab notebooks and sample or inventory management systems.

Cultural Profile

At Divergence Labs, our culture is built on a foundation of intellectual honesty, independence of thought, and a relentless commitment to excellence. We believe in fostering a collaborative environment where every team member feels empowered to contribute and grow. We are looking for individuals who embody the following characteristics and can fit in with a high-performing team of drug hunters, investors, engineers, and machine learning researchers:

Intellectual Honesty
: We value candid and open discussion. Our team admits when wrong, advocates when right, and never shies away from constructive feedback.
Bias for Action
: We take initiative and ownership of our work, actively seeking out new ideas, and taking well-researched and smart risks.
Team First Attitude
: We win as a team and lose as a team. There are "no egos" at Divergence Labs, and we understand great ideas can come from anywhere.
Independence of Thought
: We think critically and challenge assumptions. When it suits us, we develop hypotheses that may run counter to consensus, "zigging while others are zagging."
Resilience
: Drug development is a tough sport. We persevere in the face of challenge.
Embrace the Unfamiliar
: We are humbled and excited by how much there is left to learn.

Next Steps

Interested candidates can reach out to careers@divergencelabs.com with their resume and two to three sentences expressing their interest.

Divergence Labs is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences.

Job Description

The Quality Control Technician II plays a key role in ensuring that food products consistently meet internal quality expectations and regulatory food safety standards. This position focuses on routine monitoring, inspections, and data collection across production lines, helping to maintain a safe and compliant operation while supporting continuous improvement in quality assurance and quality control.

Responsibilities

Perform product temperature checks throughout production to verify compliance with food safety and quality specifications.
Conduct ATP equipment hygiene checks to confirm proper sanitation and cleanliness of production equipment.
Inspect equipment for cleanliness and sanitation readiness before and during use.
Perform Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) inspections on the production floor to ensure adherence to established standards.
Conduct sanitizer concentration verification to confirm proper dosing and effectiveness.
Measure pH and salt concentrations to ensure products meet defined quality parameters.
Perform detailed pre-operational inspections prior to production start-up to verify that all equipment and areas are ready for use.
Verify water temperatures used in production and sanitation processes to ensure compliance with established requirements.
Accurately document all inspection and test results in the appropriate systems or logs.
Report any deviations, non-conformances, or potential food safety risks promptly to quality assurance leadership.
Support running production lines after inspections are completed and cleared for operation.
Assist with basic calibration checks related to temperature, weight, and other critical control measurements as needed.
Follow established quality assurance and quality control procedures and contribute to maintaining a culture of food safety and continuous improvement.

Essential Skills

Hands-on experience in the meat industry, with familiarity with production processes and food safety considerations.
Strong understanding of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and the ability to perform GMP inspections.
Experience performing temperature checks on products and process equipment in a production environment.
Ability to conduct weight checks and basic calibration-related activities for production and quality equipment.
Experience in quality assurance and quality control within a food manufacturing setting.
Ability to perform and interpret pH readings and salt concentration measurements.
Proficiency with basic computer skills for data entry, documentation, and reporting of quality results.
High level of attention to detail and accuracy when recording data and identifying deviations.
Comfort working in both hot and cold environments, including refrigerated and freezer areas.
Ability to work flexible shifts, including early morning or daytime schedules, as assigned.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Bachelors degree in Food Science or a related field is helpful and considered an asset.
Experience in both Quality Control Technician I and II level responsibilities is beneficial.
Ability to adapt to changing schedules and assignments across different production lines.
Strong communication skills to effectively report findings and collaborate with quality assurance leadership and production teams.
Demonstrated reliability and commitment to maintaining high standards of food safety and product quality.
Interest in long-term growth opportunities within a quality and food safety career path.

Job Description

Idaho National Laboratory is hiring a well-qualified Postdoctoral Research Associate in Computational Geoscience for the Department of Critical Minerals & Geothermal Energy in the Energy and Environment Science and Technology (EES&T) directorate. This postdoctoral researcher will advance reactive transport and coupled thermal–hydraulic–mechanical–chemical (THMC) simulations emphasizing interactions among fluid flow, heat transfer, geochemical reactions, geomechanics, and evolving rock properties. Simulations will be developed using FALCON (Fracturing And Liquid CONvection) and MOOSE (Multiphysics Object-Oriented Simulation Environment), or similar tools. Research will address geological hydrogen (geohydrogen) production, electrofracturing stimulation for critical mineral recovery, enhanced geothermal systems (EGS), and carbon mineralization. Key Responsibilities

Develop reactive transport models using FALCON/MOOSE or similar tools, coupling advection, diffusion, dispersion, aqueous speciation, and mineral dissolution and precipitation with thermal, hydraulic, and mechanical processes.
Implement reaction kinetics and reactive surface area, porosity, permeability, and fracture–matrix exchange conditions; quantify species transport and elemental mass balances. Evaluate transport-limited versus reaction-limited behavior and represent mineralogical heterogeneity and evolving fluid chemistry across laboratory and reservoir scales.
Model hydrogen generation through water–rock reactions, critical mineral mobilization and recovery, and carbon mineralization; evaluate how fluid chemistry and operating conditions influence reaction progress and recovery.
Couple electrofracturing and electrohydraulic stimulation with reactive transport to assess fracture connectivity, fluid access, and mineral accessibility; simulate circulation and heat extraction in EGS.
Verify numerical implementations, calibrate and validate models against laboratory or field observations, and assess convergence, parameter sensitivity, and uncertainty.
Automate computational workflows, improve parallel performance, collaborate with experimental teams, publish findings, and contribute to research proposals.

The candidate is expected to be a strong asset to our interdisciplinary R&D team and work effectively both alone and as a team member. The candidate must be self-motivated but also take direction from other team members and peers.

Foundation in finite-element methods and nonlinear numerical solution techniques, with experience in model verification or validation.
Scientific programming in C++, Fortran, Python, or MATLAB, with ability to develop, adapt, and maintain numerical modeling components and automated simulation workflows.
A developing peer-reviewed publication record, effective communication, and ability to conduct independent research within interdisciplinary teams.

Experience with FALCON and MOOSE Porous Flow, Geochemistry, Solid Mechanics, or Phase Field capabilities, including coupling THMC processes.

Experience simulating reactive transport models, familiarity with thermodynamic databases, kinetic rate laws, and the influence of temperature and fluid composition on mineral reactivity is desirable.
Experience with nonlinear solvers, Newton’s or quasi-Newton’s methods, sparse linear algebra, preconditioning, and parallel programming using the Message Passing Interface (MPI). Scripps Research is a nonprofit biomedical institute ranked as one of the most influential in the world for its impact on innovation. We celebrated our 100-year legacy in 2024. The Xiang-Lei Yang Lab at Scripps Research seeking a motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate how a tRNA synthetase links nutrient sensing to translational control in pancreatic β-cells. By integrating mouse models, primary cells and tissues, and multi-omics approaches, the research seeks to uncover fundamental mechanisms underlying metabolic regulation and diabetes.

new_jobs.title: Research Associate / Senior Research Associate, Evidence Base (Applications Development)
new_jobs.description:
Themis Bios is building the measurement layer for modern biology. Our single-cell RNA-seq technology is designed to make transcriptomic readouts routine, quantitative, and scalable — so scientists can ask harder questions and trust the answers.

We are looking for a Research Associate or Senior Research Associate to join Applications Development and own the cell biology at the front of our workflows. This is a hands-on, bench-first role: you will grow the cells, build the models, and turn living systems into single-cell samples that read cleanly on our platform. Your first focus is the Evidence Base: running the drug-perturbation experiments behind a growing atlas of how human primary cells and organoids respond to compounds. You will work alongside our Product Development team, and your culture work and sample prep will be the foundation the rest of the applications work is built on.

It is a good fit for someone who takes real pride in cell culture and technique, wants their bench work to feed a product, and brings hands-on drug screening experience they want to build on with single-cell readouts.

What you'll do
Cell culture.
Culture primary human PBMCs (thaw, rest and T-cell activation, e.g. anti-CD3/CD28) and gut organoids, with iPSC-derived models as needed — covering media preparation, plating, passaging, expansion, and cryopreservation, all under strict sterile technique.
Model quality.
Monitor culture health, morphology, and consistency; run routine checks and keep cultures to documented, reproducible standards so downstream results are trustworthy.
Sample preparation.
Prepare single-cell and single-nucleus samples from cells, organoids, and tissue — dissociation, viability and debris management, counting, and input QC — tuned for compatibility with the Themis scRNA-seq technology.
Experiment execution.
Execute cell-culture and sample-prep experiments, and run drug-perturbation studies (drug and molecule treatments across dose and time), under the direction of senior team members.
Drug plate preparation.
Prepare compound stocks in DMSO, serial dilutions, dose–response and combination layouts, and randomized plate maps with vehicle and control wells; keep compound inventory, storage and lot records current.

Program and run liquid handlers (e.g. Agilent Bravo) for plate stamping, dilution and sample handling, and keep run logs.
Screening cadence.
Deliver about two drug plates a week on schedule, from cells to single-cell libraries, with QC at each step.
Data and records.
Generate high-quality, reproducible data and keep detailed, well-organized experimental records.
Protocols and QC.
Help turn working procedures into clear protocols and SOPs, and contribute to input-QC and sample-acceptance methods as workflows mature.
Lab operations.
Keep the lab running — inventory, reagent and consumable stocks, equipment upkeep and calibration — so experiments start on time and run clean.

What you'll bring
Bachelor's or Master's degree in cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, or a related field.
2–5 years of relevant industry or advanced academic laboratory experience (toward the upper end for the SRA level).
Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture skills and disciplined sterile technique — together with drug screening, this is the core of the role.
Hands-on drug or compound screening in mammalian cells — dose–response or plate-based assays, including preparing drug plates from stocks.
Experience with primary immune cells (PBMCs preferred) and one or more of: 3D / organoid culture, or iPSC culture and differentiation.
Sample-prep experience — dissociating cells, organoids, or tissue into high-quality single-cell suspensions, or a clear aptitude to learn it quickly.
Careful technique with complex biological workflows, and a track record of generating reproducible data and troubleshooting experiments.
Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and clear documentation habits.
Comfortable in a dynamic startup environment with evolving priorities.

Strongly preferred
Experience with single-cell genomics workflows (e.g. scRNA-seq, droplet or bead-based systems, barcoding / cell-hashing methods).
Experience writing or adapting liquid-handler methods (e.g. Agilent Bravo, Hamilton, Echo) or other high-throughput sample handling.

Nice to have
Experience with NGS library prep and QC methods (Bioanalyzer, TapeStation, Qubit, fragment analysis).
Basic data-analysis skills (e.g. Python, R, or standard analysis tools) for exploring experimental results.
Prior work in an assay-development, applications, or product-development lab.

What success looks like
Cultures and models are healthy, consistent, and ready when the team needs them.
Single-cell samples go into the workflow at high quality, with QC that holds up run to run.
Data is reproducible and records are clear enough that others can build on the work.
Throughput and reliability of the applications team go up because of how you run the bench.
Drug plates go out on schedule, about two a week, with plate-map and dosing errors near zero and vehicle-control variability within spec.
Each new model and plate workflow has an SOP someone else can run from.
You operate with growing independence, flag issues early, and reinforce a culture of rigor and accountability.

Divergence Labs is hiring a full-time Research Associate / Associate Scientist to run the laboratory data generation work that feeds our machine learning models for antibody and biologics design. We are seeking a capable candidate with a track record of scientific and professional achievement, including but not limited to 1 – 3 years of academic or industry experience in a molecular biology or protein science laboratory. The role is based on-site in San Francisco, CA, and works directly with our Machine Learning and Engineering team.

Divergence Labs is a biotechnology company on a mission to reshape standard of care across all disease areas. Founded in 2025 by an interdisciplinary team of biotechnology investors, drug hunters, hardware engineers, and machine learning scientists, we have assembled a high-performance team that unites investment acumen, world-class protein engineering, advanced computational research, and translational medicine to build repeatable methods for discovering new medicines which transform patient care. Divergence has presence across San Francisco, CA, Minneapolis, MN, New York, NY, and Cambridge, UK. Although we have not publicly disclosed our financing details, Divergence is well capitalized and backed by world-leading investors, each of whom are among the earliest investors in companies such as Isomorphic Labs, Xaira Therapeutics, Coefficient Bio/Anthropic, and Chai Discovery, among others. We are among a select set of biotechnology companies with a strategic relationship with Anthropic.

We are committed to identifying, developing, and rewarding world-class talent, and, as such, all positions at Divergence Labs come with market-leading compensation.

The Role

We are hiring a hands-on Research Associate / Associate Scientist to be the experimental half of our design loop in San Francisco. Our machine learning team designs antibodies computationally; this role turns those designs into physical molecules and measured data, and returns that data to the models that learn from it. The San Francisco group is small and tightly coupled: machine learning scientists, software engineers and hardware engineers working alongside the bench scientists who generate the experimental readouts their models depend on.

You will work day to day at the bench running our data generation pipeline: building designed sequences from synthetic DNA, expressing the encoded proteins, and measuring binding. The quality, consistency and turnaround of what you produce sets the pace for model development and pipeline execution, and the people who use your data one desk away.

This is also a role with room to grow. You will be trained on our core methods, work closely with engineers who are automating them, and have the opportunity to take on greater ownership of assay development, automation and data analysis as the pipeline scales.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are looking for a capable, motivated bench scientist who wants to learn fast in a small, integrated team and contribute from day one. Your background should include:

Solid hands-on molecular biology and protein experience
: Confident and independent at the bench with routine molecular biology, protein expression and plate-based assays, executed consistently and on schedule.
A data-minded, reliable working style
: You treat every plate as a dataset someone else will train on: consistent execution, careful controls and records, and problems flagged and troubleshooted.
Curiosity about machine learning and automation
: Keen to work at the interface of the bench and the model, and to grow into greater ownership as the pipeline scales.

Key Responsibilities

Run the data generation pipeline
: Execute our build-and-test workflow end to end, from synthetic DNA through expressed protein to binding measurements, on a regular weekly cadence.
Build designed sequences
: Carry out the molecular biology that turns computational designs into testable constructs: PCR, assembly, pooled and arrayed library handling, and sequence verification.
Express and quantify proteins
: Produce antibody fragments and target antigens in small-scale, plate-based formats, and confirm expression and quality before measurement.
Measure binding at scale
: Run high-throughput binding and kinetics assays (e.g., biolayer interferometry), including instrument setup, controls, and first-pass data review.
Deliver clean, structured data
: Record sample tracking, metadata and results in the formats our machine learning team consumes, and flag failed or ambiguous runs before they reach a model.
Operate and help improve automation
: Run liquid handlers and plate-based instruments, and work with our engineers to raise throughput, reduce cost per datapoint and shorten turnaround.
Troubleshoot and iterate
: Identify the source of failed runs, test fixes, and help refine protocols and SOPs as methods mature.
Keep the lab running
: Prepare reagents, manage consumables and ordering, maintain shared equipment, and coordinate with external vendors where needed.
Embody good lab citizenship

Job Title: Quality Control Technician II

Job Description

The Quality Control Technician II plays a key role in ensuring that food products consistently meet internal quality expectations and regulatory food safety standards. This position focuses on routine monitoring, inspections, and data collection across production lines, helping to maintain a safe and compliant operation while supporting continuous improvement in quality assurance and quality control.

Responsibilities

Perform product temperature checks throughout production to verify compliance with food safety and quality specifications.
Conduct ATP equipment hygiene checks to confirm proper sanitation and cleanliness of production equipment.
Inspect equipment for cleanliness and sanitation readiness before and during use.
Perform Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) inspections on the production floor to ensure adherence to established standards.
Conduct sanitizer concentration verification to confirm proper dosing and effectiveness.
Measure pH and salt concentrations to ensure products meet defined quality parameters.
Perform detailed pre-operational inspections prior to production start-up to verify that all equipment and areas are ready for use.
Verify water temperatures used in production and sanitation processes to ensure compliance with established requirements.
Accurately document all inspection and test results in the appropriate systems or logs.
Report any deviations, non-conformances, or potential food safety risks promptly to quality assurance leadership.
Support running production lines after inspections are completed and cleared for operation.
Assist with basic calibration checks related to temperature, weight, and other critical control measurements as needed.
Follow established quality assurance and quality control procedures and contribute to maintaining a culture of food safety and continuous improvement.

Essential Skills

Hands-on experience in the meat industry, with familiarity with production processes and food safety considerations.
Strong understanding of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and the ability to perform GMP inspections.
Experience performing temperature checks on products and process equipment in a production environment.
Ability to conduct weight checks and basic calibration-related activities for production and quality equipment.
Experience in quality assurance and quality control within a food manufacturing setting.
Ability to perform and interpret pH readings and salt concentration measurements.
Proficiency with basic computer skills for data entry, documentation, and reporting of quality results.
High level of attention to detail and accuracy when recording data and identifying deviations.
Comfort working in both hot and cold environments, including refrigerated and freezer areas.
Ability to work flexible shifts, including early morning or daytime schedules, as assigned.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Bachelors degree in Food Science or a related field is helpful and considered an asset.
Experience in both Quality Control Technician I and II level responsibilities is beneficial.
Ability to adapt to changing schedules and assignments across different production lines.
Strong communication skills to effectively report findings and collaborate with quality assurance leadership and production teams.
Demonstrated reliability and commitment to maintaining high standards of food safety and product quality.
Interest in long-term growth opportunities within a quality and food safety career path.

Work schedules are flexible, with typical shifts such as 3:00 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. or 7:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the ability to adjust as operational needs change. The environment supports long-term career growth opportunities following an initial contract period, with exposure to a structured quality assurance and quality control culture focused on continuous improvement and regulatory compliance.

Job Description

The mission of the UCSF Department of Surgery is threefold: to develop the next generation of leaders in surgery; to provide outstanding quality clinical care that is cost effective, yet compassionate; and to make significant advances in scientific knowledge and clinical practice through basic and clinical research. Care of patients is what attracted our faculty and residents to surgery, and it continues to be our main focus. The Department is comprised of seven divisions including Adult Cardiothoracic Surgery, General Surgery, Pediatric Cardiothoracic Surgery, Pediatric Surgery, Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery, Transplant Surgery, and Vascular & Endovascular Surgery.

The UCSF-ITL is a high complexity clinical laboratory that performs tests and provides services that support solid organ (kidney, heart, lung, liver, pancreas, islet, etc.) and hematopoietic stem cell (blood, marrow, cord blood, etc.) transplant programs. The laboratory is CLIA certified and is licensed by the states of California and New York. The lab is also certified as a free-standing-histocompatibility laboratory by the Centers of Medicare and Medicaid (CMS). The laboratory serves as a core laboratory for the NIH Immune Tolerance Network and provides support for several national clinical trials.

Perform laboratory functions that support solid organ and blood & marrow transplant programs. Functions include on-call responsibilities for the deceased donor transplant programs; perform infectious disease testing; data entry of patient and sample information into various systems, prepare cell subsets; isolate DNA; HLA type by various methods; crossmatch by flow cytometry method; test and identify HLA antibodies; chimerism monitoring and other HLA-related tests; assist in managing samples (store, retrieve, and aliquot samples); perform quality control and routine maintenance of various laboratory equipment; analyze and report laboratory data; order supplies, repairs, and other services; answer phones and perform other duties as assigned.

Tidy and orderly

Advance degree (Masters or doctorate) in a relevant field (e.g., immunology, blood banking, and biochemistry)
Experience with QC/QA/QS in a clinical laboratory setting
